```bash
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding     # keyless memory, no server needed
gbrain doctor --json                   # inspect diagnostics and any warnings
```

**The first-run settings.** Init applies its defaults and exits 0; nothing waits
for an answer. When no agent is connected yet it prints a `harness_wiring`
notice: connecting gbrain to the agent you run in is part of the install, so do
it now (Step 5), not after the user replies. It also prints the settings in
effect once, as an `[AGENT]` block (`gbrain init --json`: a notice of kind
`ask` with `decisions[]`):

| Setting | What the user can change | In effect |
|---|---|---|
| `search_mode` | `conservative`, `balanced` or `tokenmax`, with the cost matrix (Step 3.5) | the mode init applied, with its reason |
| `writeback` | whether you save salient facts from conversations without being asked | off; gbrain recommends `salient`, which the user opts into |
| `skills_scaffold` | optional bundled skills in the agent workspace | skip |
| `upkeep` | free upkeep while the agent's session is open | on |

Connect first, then report the install and relay the bundle's `user_message`
in that reply, as the settings in effect and how to change them. Apply an
answer with the command its option names whenever the user gives one. Details:
[first run](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run).
## Step 3.5: Tell the user which search mode is in effect (DO NOT SKIP)

This is the `search_mode` setting from the first-run settings.
`gbrain init` auto-applied a default search mode: `tokenmax` with a chat key
(Anthropic, OpenAI or Google), `balanced` with a ready reranker but no chat key,
and `conservative` when your subagent tier is Haiku-class or neither exists. The init output
included the cost matrix below preceded by `[AGENT]` markers. Don't accept it
silently, and don't stop the install to ask either: on every harness, connect
gbrain first (with `gbrain setup <harness>` or the `harness_wiring` step), then
show the matrix and the applied mode in the reply that reports the install, as
a choice the user can make at any time, and run
`gbrain config set search.mode <mode>` when they pick one.

If you already know the operator's choice, record it at install time instead:
`gbrain init --search-mode <conservative|balanced|tokenmax>` stores it as the
operator's (`search.mode_source: operator`) and init asks no `search_mode`
question. On an existing brain with a different mode it refuses unless you pass
`--force`.

If skipped, minimal defaults are installed automatically.

## Opt-ins

The default install (keyless PGLite, no repo) adds nothing: no daemon, service
unit, cron entry, connector or dream schedule, and self-upgrade stays `notify`
(it reports releases and installs none). An upgrade never installs autopilot on
a brain without one. Turn each on only when the user asks:

- **Keys and embeddings:** the key (Step 2), then
  `gbrain init --force --embedding-model voyage:voyage-4 --embedding-dimensions 1024`.
- **Autopilot** (Postgres): `gbrain autopilot --install --repo <path>`; PGLite uses `gbrain serve`.
- **Dream schedule:** cron `0 2 * * * <wrapper> dream` ([wrapper](docs/guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended)).
- **Connectors:** `gbrain connectors auth <provider>` ([guide](docs/guides/chat-connectors.md)).
- **Auto-upgrade:** `gbrain config set self_upgrade.mode auto`.
- **Release channel:** `gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel alpha` (every release) or `stable`.

## Step 7: Recurring Jobs

Optional: skip this entire step for memory-only installs. Ask before scheduling
capture, enrichment, maintenance or a service; do not infer consent from a
successful install or from a health recommendation.

An open `gbrain serve` already runs the free upkeep while its agent is idle
(`gbrain maintain --status` shows the last run). For the jobs below, set up
using your platform's scheduler (OpenClaw cron, Railway cron, crontab), or skip the
platform glue entirely with `gbrain autopilot --install` (built-in self-maintaining daemon).


## Step 8: Integrations

Run `gbrain integrations list`, then `gbrain integrations show <id>` for one recipe.
Each recipe is a self-contained installer. It tells you what credentials to ask for, how to validate, and what cron
to register. Ask the user which integrations they want (email, calendar, voice, Twitter).

Verify: `gbrain integrations doctor` (after at least one is configured)

### A bot that answers in channels or shared sessions

Every successful MCP tool call except `recall`, `extract_facts` and
`forget_fact` can carry a `_meta.brain_hot_memory` block. It holds recent
facts from the connection's own source: a token's write source (the first id
of its source grant), a stdio server's resolved source, or `default`. For a
member token whose first source is that member's private source, the block
holds that member's own facts, such as preferences from a direct message. The
grant still holds: the block never draws on a source the connection can't
read. But the harness may put it into its context, so the member's facts can
reach a channel reply other people read.

A harness running a channel or other shared session should set
`_meta.hot_memory: "off"` on each tool call, on the MCP request beside
`arguments` or inside the arguments. That call then carries no block. One
member's direct-message session can keep it. Details:
[MCP_META_CHANNELS.md](docs/protocol/MCP_META_CHANNELS.md#brain_hot_memory-when-it-appears-and-how-to-turn-it-off).

closing "answer" sentence on heartbeat, cron and exec-completion turns). The plugin is
self-contained (the rule text is in its code; it reads and calls nothing) and

`openclaw mcp` has two jobs:

- run OpenClaw as an MCP server with `openclaw mcp serve`
- manage OpenClaw-managed outbound MCP server definitions with `list`, `show`, `status`, `doctor`, `probe`, `add`, `set`, `configure`, `tools`, `login`, `logout`, `reload`, and `unset`

`serve` is OpenClaw acting as an MCP server. The other subcommands are OpenClaw acting as an MCP client-side registry for servers its own runtimes may consume later.

<Note>
  `list`, `show`, `set`, and `unset` only read and write OpenClaw-managed `mcp.servers` entries in OpenClaw config. They do not include mcporter servers from `config/mcporter.json`; use `mcporter list` for that registry.
</Note>

Use [`openclaw acp`](/cli/acp) when OpenClaw should host a coding harness session itself and route that runtime through ACP.

## Choose the right MCP path

| Goal                                                                | Use                                                                  | Why                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Let an external MCP client read/send OpenClaw channel conversations | `openclaw mcp serve`                                                 | OpenClaw is the MCP server and exposes Gateway-backed conversations over stdio.                                 |
| Save third-party MCP servers for OpenClaw-managed agent runs        | `openclaw mcp add`, `set`, `configure`, `tools`, `login`             | OpenClaw is the MCP client-side registry and later projects those servers into eligible runtimes.               |
| Check a saved server without running an agent turn                  | `openclaw mcp status`, `doctor`, `probe`                             | `status` and `doctor` inspect config; `probe` opens a live MCP connection and lists capabilities.               |
| Edit MCP config from a browser                                      | Control UI `/settings/mcp` (`/mcp` alias)                            | The page shows inventory, enablement, OAuth/filter summaries, command hints, and a scoped `mcp` editor.         |
| Give Codex app-server a scoped native MCP server                    | `mcp.servers.<name>.codex`                                           | The `codex` block only affects Codex app-server thread projection and is stripped before native config handoff. |
| Run ACP-hosted harness sessions                                     | [`openclaw acp`](/cli/acp) and [ACP Agents](/tools/acp-agents-setup) | ACP bridge mode does not accept per-session MCP server injection; configure gateway/plugin bridges instead.     |

<Tip>
If you are not sure which path you need, start with `openclaw mcp status --verbose`. It shows what OpenClaw has saved without starting any MCP servers.
